display.title: Reb Levi Yitzchak's Secret Midnight Chuppah
display.summary_short: In Communist Yekaterinoslav, the Rebbe's father makes a secret midnight chuppah and must ask a Communist informer to complete the minyan.
display.summary_long: In the 1930s in Yekaterinoslav, where the Rebbe's father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak, was the Rav, the Communists threw Jews into prison for teaching Torah and paid informers to report on them. Even the Jewish superintendent of Reb Levik's building was hired to write down who came and went. Reb Levik kept teaching in secret. One night at eleven, a woman arrives from a faraway city: her daughter and her Jewish groom both work for the government and will agree to a Jewish wedding only if it is secret and performed by Reb Levik. At midnight the veiled bride and the groom in a leather coat arrive. Reb Levik gathers trustworthy men but is one short of a minyan, so he calls up the superintendent. Surprised, the man locks the door and pulls down the shades himself. With a dark velvet cloth for a chuppah and no candles, the wedding takes place, and the couple hurries away. Then two of the men take out their Communist Party cards and tell Reb Levik these mean nothing anymore; they do teshuvah and help him spread Torah.
display.lesson: Mesiras nefesh for a mitzvah can bring even those who seem far away back to Hashem.

advisories.note: Jews were jailed for teaching Torah, and informers were paid to report on them.
